summary_md:
# 585. Inge Heydorns jätteguide till AI-aktier

**Feed**: sparpodden  
**Published**: 2026-10-28  
**Market Sentiment**: Positive

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

Inge Heydorn, a tech fund manager, argues that AI demand remains stronger than ever and that the recent sell-off in AI stocks is mostly driven by higher interest rates and financing worries, not by any change in fundamentals. He sees memory chips as a structural shortage likely to last until 2030 or later, and Micron, priced at roughly 5x earnings, as his preferred way to own it. Financing, political pushback against data centers and power shortages are named as the main risks, but he believes the market is too afraid of AI right now.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 MU — Micron | **BUY** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 85%

Guest's main memory holding; P/E ~5, 85% gross margin; buybacks from 9 Dec; added after the dip.

#### Reasoning

Guest opinion (fund manager). Memory shortage expected to last to 2030+. Contract prices have not yet rolled into reported numbers, and HBM4E lifts prices from January. The market is pricing a cyclical downturn that he thinks is far away. At P/E ~5 the price is earned back in a few years. Buyback could approach $135bn over 12 months. Pure-play and US governance justify a small premium over Samsung/Hynix.

#### Sell Triggers

- memory supply catches up with demand and cyclical oversupply arrives
- AI capex financing dries up
- valuation re-rates to premium levels

> *"Vårt val har varit Micron. Skälet till det är att det är amerikanskt."*

---

### 🟢 NVDA — Nvidia | **BUY** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 80%

Guest held the maximum ~9.8% weight before the August report. 70% growth guide likely beaten. SpaceX orders give a strong Q4.

#### Reasoning

Guest opinion. Nvidia guided 70% growth next year and could reach 90-100% as capacity grows. GPU compute prices have risen 15-16 days in a row despite the sell-off. Hyperscaler and neocloud demand (SpaceX, CoreWeave backstop) is very large.

#### Sell Triggers

- financing for data centers collapses
- political blocking of US data centers
- memory shortage limits shipments

> *"vi har alla Nvidia vi kan. Så vi ligger på 9,8% i fonden."*

---

### 🟡 MSFT — Microsoft | **HOLD** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 65%

Large fund holding, trimmed only because of UCITS limits after outperforming.

#### Reasoning

Guest opinion. Microsoft held up better than the market and hit regulatory concentration limits, forcing small net sales. This is not a negative fundamental view: Microsoft is a strong customer for neoclouds and its new Maia chip needs more memory.

#### Sell Triggers

- AI demand from enterprises slows
- capex financing becomes costly

> *"Då måste vi ligga och netto-sälja Microsoft lite grann."*

---

### 🟢 ABB — ABB | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Guest calls it an absolute long-term winner on power/grid shortage and automation, though his fund does not own it.

#### Reasoning

Guest opinion. The main AI bottleneck is power: old grids need new capacity, transformers and electricians, and automation and robotics are growing. Guest says it is a long-term winning trend but does not follow or own ABB, so conviction is moderate.

#### Sell Triggers

- grid investment slows
- AI data-center build-out stalls

> *"Jag tycker att det är en vinnare, absolut."*

---

### 🟠 CRWV — CoreWeave | **WATCH** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Capacity sold out for 6 years with an Nvidia backstop. Most beaten-down name. Guest views the financing risk as overstated.

#### Reasoning

Guest opinion. Contracts with Meta and Microsoft and Nvidia's purchase guarantee secure long-term revenue. Short-term risk is the build-out cost on older, cheap contracts ($13-15bn/GW vs $40-45bn now) plus financing and political delays. Rising compute prices lift the value of existing capacity.

#### Sell Triggers

- data-center construction delays
- financing costs spike
- key customer default

> *"Och Corevid är den som har blivit mest nedtryckt just nu."*

---

### 🟠 000660.KS — SK Hynix | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 40%

P/E under 4 and strong buybacks, but guest avoids it because SK Group controls capital allocation.

#### Reasoning

Guest opinion. Benefits from the same memory upcycle as Micron, but Hynix's capital allocation is decided by SK Group, a governance risk. The fund prefers Micron.

#### Sell Triggers

- group-level capital misallocation
- memory oversupply

> *"kapitalallokeringen i Heinix bestäms ju inte hos Heinix."*
